messages:

Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging — clarification for three-cloud launch

Mina — thanks again for the sync earlier. Azure PM here. We need to lock the SKU/region decisions so our marketplace ops teams can queue the listings and co-sell leads routing. Specific asks from our side: 

- Which single SKU will we surface as the canary for each cloud (smallest config + free trial)
- Region gating: do we require EU data residency for Acme's onboarding?
- Any differences in packaging strings or metering that will affect offer acceptance (Azure wants a clear monthly seat vs vCPU SKU)

Can you confirm by EOD Monday? We have an internal cutover window the week of May 3. Attaching the draft checklist we discussed.

Attachments: launch_checklist_draft.docx (referenced)

—Tim
Azure Marketplace Partnerships

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Harris <tim@azuremarketplace.com>, Alex Huang <alex@aws-partner.com>, Sara Malik <sara@gcp-partner.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging — clarification for three-cloud launch

Tim / Alex / Sara — thanks for the clear list. I captured recommendations below after consulting product and GTM. I attached a compact launch matrix and the co-sell handover checklist for ops. High level: keep SKU parity where possible but optimize the canonical canary SKU per cloud to match each marketplace's preferred metering model.

Recommendations (canary SKU, primary region, packaging summary):

- Azure: SKU "Redwood-Inference-Basic" (1xvCPU-equivalent instance; 30k tokens/mo, 14-day free trial) — Primary region: West US; EU support via Azure SE with data processed in West Europe region; pricing strings use monthly subscription + overage per token.

- AWS: SKU "redwood.small-inference" (tied to instance family for easier AMI listing; pay-as-you-go hourly + token metering) — Primary region: us-west-2; EU canary: eu-west-1 but we avoid immediate APAC rollout for the canary.

- GCP: SKU "redwood-inference-starter" (subscription with committed spend option; quota-based metering) — Primary region: us-central1; GCP accepts trial credits via promotions rather than a 14-day trial UI.

Notes on parity and differences:
- Offer strings will differ slightly: Azure requires explicit "monthly subscription" text; AWS allows instance-style descriptors in the title; GCP needs the commitment tier in metadata. We should keep the functional product description identical and maintain the same model version and quantization profile for canaries to ensure consistent performance claims.

- EU data residency for Acme: Acme requested EU-only processing. For the initial canary we can use Azure West Europe (for Azure) and AWS eu-west-1 (for AWS). GCP EU region can be enabled but plan a delayed listing (phase 2) to avoid submission rejections.

Action items / next steps: 
1) Ben / Karthik: finalize the short launch matrix (I attached v1) with SKU IDs and marketplace submission owners.
2) Ben: confirm lead-routing tags we should push to marketplace integrations for co-sell (e.g., "acme-trial-2027") so you get auto-forwarding to Acme's AE in Salesforce.
3) Ben + Karthik: coordinate with legal on Azure subscription wording.
4) Mina: I'll consolidate and send the official handover doc to partners and Acme.

Attachments: 2027-04-25_redwood_three-cloud_launch_matrix_v1.xlsx; co-sell-handover-checklist.md

Thanks — Mina
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Ben / Karthik — forwarding the partner thread. Short and urgent: we need the matrix completed by EOD Tuesday so partners can file their marketplace submissions early next week. See my inline asks from the earlier note. 

Quick priorities for the matrix (I added bold in the spreadsheet):
- SKU external title (exact string for each cloud)
- Marketplace-friendly billing type (subscription, hourly, committed)
- Primary and fallback region mapping per account class (Acme = EU residency required)
- Lead routing tag and HubSpot/ Salesforce mapping

Lauren — tagging you for a pragmatic go/no-go on exceptions (e.g., allowing a GCP delayed EU canary) so I can close the loop with Tim and Sara.

Thanks — Mina

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Mina / team — go ahead with the proposed approach. Approvals and constraints:

- Approve Azure and AWS canaries for initial EU processing for Acme (use West Europe / eu-west-1 respectively).
- GCP EU listing delayed to phase 2 (we'll document the timing and the trigger in the handover checklist).
- Exception: if a partner flags a hard rejection from marketplace ops, escalate to me and I'll intervene.

Please land the matrix and the routing tags. Once Ben confirms routing tags, Mina please send the consolidated handover to partners and cc me.

—Lauren
VP, Partnerships & Channels
